title: Multi-Agent Task Coordination System
description: Build a multi-agent system where specialized agents coordinate on shared tasks via explicit message contracts: a planner/worker topology with typed handoffs, state isolation, loop detection, and an evaluation comparing coordination against a single-agent baseline on the same task set.
learningObjectives: Define typed message contracts between at least three agent roles
Isolate each agent's state so failures don't cascade silently
Detect and break coordination loops deterministically
Compare multi-agent vs single-agent performance honestly on identical tasks

milestones.title: Typed message contracts
milestones.objective: Define message schemas (task, result, query, escalation) validated on send/receive.

milestones.title: Planner/worker topology
milestones.objective: Implement planner decomposition,≥2 specialized workers, and an aggregator; each with isolated state.
milestones.expectedOutput: A task of ≥6 subtasks executes end-to-end.

milestones.title: Loop detection & escalation
milestones.objective: Detect repeated exchanges (e.g. same pair twice without progress) and escalate to human or abort.

milestones.title: Baseline comparison
milestones.objective: Run the same ≥5 tasks single-agent vs multi-agent; report quality, latency, and cost per task.
milestones.expectedOutput: Per-task table; honest claim about where multi-agent helped or hurt.

categories.excellentExpectation: Analysis of task types where one wins

architecture: shared task ledger, isolated per-agent memory
constraints: No direct agent-to-agent side channels; everything via typed bus
hints: The most common failure is parallel workers editing shared state: prove isolation or lower expectations honestly
